ask: What drives FFA and OFA apart?

nodes.label: scrambled face parts
nodes.question: Calibration: does scrambling the face parts cost FFA more than OFA, as Liu, Harris and Kanwisher (2010) found?

nodes.label: two tone mooney faces
nodes.question: Calibration: does a Mooney two-tone face spare FFA relative to OFA, as Rossion et al. (2011) found?

nodes.label: head turned 30 degrees
nodes.question: Does turning the same head 30 degrees away from frontal cost OFA more than FFA (H3), or FFA more than OFA (H4)?

nodes.label: averted gaze faces
nodes.question: Does averting the gaze of the same faces move OFA more than FFA (H9), or leave them parallel (H10)?

nodes.label: stripped to internal face
nodes.question: Does stripping the hair, head outline and background (internal face only) favour OFA over FFA?

nodes.label: negated face eyes restored
nodes.question: In a contrast-negated face, does restoring positive polarity to the eyes alone favour FFA (H12)?

nodes.label: lit from below
nodes.question: Does lighting the same faces from below, against the light-from-above prior, cost FFA more than OFA?

params.prompt: relight the face with a single light source from directly below the chin; keep identity, pose, expression, framing, hair and background the same
no change

nodes.label: fur covering human faces
nodes.question: Does covering the same human faces in short fur, with features and shape kept, move them toward OFA?

params.prompt: cover the skin of the face with short realistic fur; keep the human eyes, nose, mouth, face shape, identity, pose, framing, lighting and background the same
no change

nodes.label: colour loss alone
nodes.question: Is n05's FFA drop carried by the loss of colour alone?

nodes.label: grey background replacing scene
nodes.question: Does replacing the scene behind the same person with plain grey cost FFA more than OFA?

params.prompt: replace the background with a plain flat mid-grey; keep the person, face, hair, clothing, identity, pose, framing, colour and lighting the same
no change

nodes.label: hair removed from faces
nodes.question: Does removing the hair (and with it the usual head outline) cost FFA more than OFA?

params.prompt: remove all hair from the head so the person is completely bald; keep the face, eyebrows, identity, expression, pose, framing, lighting, clothing and background the same
no change

nodes.label: photograph shrunk in frame
nodes.question: Does shrinking the same photograph in the frame cost FFA more than OFA?

nodes.label: animal faces without fur
nodes.question: Is OFA's hold on furred faces carried by fur? Remove it from animal faces.

params.prompt: make the animal completely hairless with smooth bare skin like a sphynx cat; keep the face shape, eyes, pose, framing, lighting and background the same
no change

nodes.label: fine grain on skin
nodes.question: Does fine, non-fur grain added to human facial skin favour OFA, as fur did on resnet50?

params.prompt: give the skin of the face a coarse rough texture with large visible pores and fine grain; keep identity, age, face shape, expression, pose, framing, colour, lighting and background the same
no change

nodes.label: head turned 45 degrees
nodes.question: Does a larger head turn (45 degrees) push n03's lean past the bound and decide between H3 and H4?

nodes.label: cyclops face one eye
nodes.question: Does a cyclops face (one central eye) favour FFA through having fewer parts, or OFA?

params.prompt: replace the two eyes with a single realistic human eye centred above the nose; keep the nose, mouth, eyebrows, skin, identity, pose, framing, lighting and background the same
no change

nodes.label: full profile face
nodes.question: Does a full profile, made by the prompted editor against a 'no change' arm, cost OFA more than FFA, and so separate H3 from H4 without n16's confound?

params.prompt: turn the head to a full side profile facing left; keep the identity, expression, hair, clothing, lighting, framing and background the same
no change

nodes.label: faces turned upside down
nodes.question: Does turning the same faces upside down cost FFA more (the inversion account) or OFA more (an upright two-dimensional layout template)?

nodes.label: both eyes enlarged
nodes.question: Does enlarging both eyes on photographs (part size up, layout kept) favour OFA, as H2's size clause says, or FFA, through the eye region (H12)?

params.prompt: enlarge both eyes to about twice their size, keeping them realistic and in the same place; keep the nose, mouth, eyebrows, identity, expression, pose, framing, lighting and background the same
no change

nodes.label: eye spacing widened
nodes.question: Does widening the eye spacing, with every part intact, cost FFA more than OFA (second-order configuration)?

params.prompt: move the two eyes noticeably further apart, keeping their size and shape; keep the nose, mouth, eyebrows, identity, expression, pose, framing, lighting and background the same
no change

nodes.label: wide open mouth
nodes.question: Does a wide-open mouth (a changeable part state other than gaze) move OFA more than FFA, deciding between H9 and H10?

params.prompt: open the mouth wide so the teeth show; keep the eyes, eyebrows, identity, pose, framing, lighting and background the same
no change

nodes.label: three quarter view
nodes.question: Does a three-quarter view (about 45 degrees) made by the same editor cost OFA more than FFA, at a smaller size than the full profile?

params.prompt: turn the head to a three-quarter view facing left, with both eyes still visible; keep the identity, expression, hair, clothing, lighting, tight framing and background the same
no change

nodes.label: one eye hidden
nodes.question: Does hiding one eye in a frontal face reproduce n19's OFA loss without any turn of the head?

params.prompt: cover the person's left eye with a plain black eye patch; keep the other eye, identity, expression, pose, framing, lighting and background the same
no change

nodes.label: profile framing expression held
nodes.question: Does the profile still cost OFA more when framing and expression are held, removing n19's extra-body and lost-smile side effects?

params.prompt: turn the head to a full side profile facing left with a neutral closed-mouth expression; keep a tight crop on the head with no extra shoulders or background showing; keep the identity, hair and lighting the same
keep the head facing the camera with a neutral closed-mouth expression; keep a tight crop on the head with no extra shoulders or background showing; keep the identity, hair and lighting the same

nodes.label: profile on animal faces
nodes.question: Does the profile cost OFA more on animal faces too, or is the effect specific to human faces?

params.prompt: turn the animal's head to a full side profile facing left; keep the same animal, fur, framing, lighting and background
no change

nodes.label: in plane face rotation
nodes.question: Does a 90-degree in-plane rotation give part of the inversion effect (a graded upright template) or none of it?

nodes.label: faces with closed eyes
nodes.question: Do closed eyes (no eye contrast, both eyes still in place) cost OFA more, as an eye-pair account says, or FFA more, through the eye-region luminance?

nodes.label: clean 30 degree turn
nodes.question: Does a clean head turn of about 30 degrees (LivePortrait, same framing, no body added, expression unchanged) cost OFA more than FFA?

nodes.label: head roll upright frame
nodes.question: Does turning the head within an upright frame (roll), with the background unrotated, cost OFA more, or does the rotation effect need the whole frame turned?

nodes.label: graded rotation angle
nodes.question: Is the clip_rn50 rotation effect graded: does 45 degrees give part of the 90-degree difference?

nodes.label: rotated objects no faces
nodes.question: Control for n29: does a 90-degree rotation of objects with no face also lower OFA and raise EBA and FBA on clip_rn50?

nodes.label: downward head tilt
nodes.question: Does a downward head tilt (pitch), which keeps both eyes visible, cost OFA more than FFA?

nodes.label: cubist face profile outline
nodes.question: In a cubist face that shows a profile nose and jaw with both eyes drawn frontally, does OFA keep its response (eye pair) or lose it (profile outline)?

params.prompt: repaint as a Picasso-style cubist portrait where the nose and jaw are seen in side profile but both eyes are drawn as if seen from the front; keep the identity, hair colour, framing and background
repaint as a Picasso-style cubist portrait with the whole face seen from the front, both eyes frontal; keep the identity, hair colour, framing and background

nodes.label: clean 45 degree turn
nodes.question: Does a larger clean head turn (45 degrees of yaw, LivePortrait) push OFA's extra cost past the bound on both backbones?

nodes.label: cubist repainted photographs
nodes.question: Is n37's style effect real: does repainting the same photographs as cubist portraits cost FFA more than OFA, against the photographs through the editor unchanged?

params.prompt: repaint as a Picasso-style cubist portrait with the face seen from the front; keep the identity, hair colour, pose, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: cartoon faces made realistic
nodes.question: Does rendering cartoon faces as realistic photographs lift FFA relative to OFA, or do the added fine edges and texture lift OFA?

params.prompt: render this cartoon face as a realistic photograph of a real person; keep the same hairstyle, hair colour, eye colour, glasses, face shape, pose, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: fine detail blurred
nodes.question: Does removing fine spatial detail (blur) from the same faces cost OFA more, through lost part edges, or FFA more, through lost photographic surface?

nodes.label: human to chimpanzee faces
nodes.question: Does turning the same human faces into chimpanzee faces cost FFA more than OFA, or are both indifferent to species when the frontal portrait is kept?

params.prompt: turn the person into a realistic chimpanzee; keep the same head pose, framing, lighting and background
no change

nodes.label: white marble face
nodes.question: Does a white marble version of the same face (texture and pigment gone, shape and shading kept) favour FFA or OFA?

params.prompt: make the face and hair a white marble statue; keep the face shape, expression, pose, lighting, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: tile mosaic face
nodes.question: Does a tile mosaic of the face favour OFA through its added tile edges, or leave the pair parallel because the frontal layout is kept?

params.prompt: render the face as an ancient Roman mosaic of small stone tiles; keep the face layout, pose, colours, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: held out cubist repaint
nodes.question: Does it hold on held-out images, on every backbone and under the judge: Is n37's style effect real: does repainting the same photographs as cubist portraits cost FFA more than OFA, against the photographs through the editor unchanged?

params.prompt: repaint as a Picasso-style cubist portrait with the face seen from the front; keep the identity, hair colour, pose, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: held out cartoon realistic
nodes.question: Does it hold on held-out images, on every backbone and under the judge: Does rendering cartoon faces as realistic photographs lift FFA relative to OFA, or do the added fine edges and texture lift OFA?

params.prompt: render this cartoon face as a realistic photograph of a real person; keep the same hairstyle, hair colour, eye colour, glasses, face shape, pose, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: held out chimpanzee faces
nodes.question: Does it hold on held-out images, on every backbone and under the judge: Does turning the same human faces into chimpanzee faces cost FFA more than OFA, or are both indifferent to species when the frontal portrait is kept?

params.prompt: turn the person into a realistic chimpanzee; keep the same head pose, framing, lighting and background
no change

nodes.label: cubist background only
nodes.question: Does the cubist background alone, with the face left a photograph, cost FFA more than OFA?

params.prompt: replace only the background with a multicoloured cubist pattern of flat angular painted shapes; keep the face, hair, clothing, identity, pose, head size and framing exactly as the original photograph
no change

nodes.label: cubist face photo background
nodes.question: Does a cubist face on the original photographic background still cost FFA more than OFA?

params.prompt: repaint only the face and hair as a Picasso-style cubist painting seen from the front; keep the original photographic background, head size, pose and framing unchanged
no change

nodes.label: glossy plastic doll face
nodes.question: Does a glossy plastic doll face, with skin colour kept, cost FFA more than OFA as marble did?

params.prompt: make the face and hair a glossy plastic toy doll with the same skin and hair colours; keep the face shape, expression, pose, lighting, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: classical oil painting face
nodes.question: Does a classical oil painting of the same face, with shading and colour kept, cost FFA less than cubism did, as a dose of realism?

params.prompt: render the image as a classical oil painting with visible brushwork; keep the identity, shading, colours, pose, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: human eyes animal faces
nodes.question: Do human eyes on animal faces pull them toward FFA, the converse of the chimpanzee edit?

params.prompt: replace the animal's eyes with realistic human eyes with white sclera and round irises, same size and position; keep the fur, ears, snout, pose, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: held out white marble
nodes.question: Does it hold on held-out images, on every backbone and under the judge: Does a white marble version of the same face (texture and pigment gone, shape and shading kept) favour FFA or OFA?

params.prompt: make the face and hair a white marble statue; keep the face shape, expression, pose, lighting, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: held out tile mosaic
nodes.question: Does it hold on held-out images, on every backbone and under the judge: Does a tile mosaic of the face favour OFA through its added tile edges, or leave the pair parallel because the frontal layout is kept?

params.prompt: render the face as an ancient Roman mosaic of small stone tiles; keep the face layout, pose, colours, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: held out cubist photo
nodes.question: Does it hold on held-out images, on every backbone and under the judge: Does a cubist face on the original photographic background still cost FFA more than OFA?

params.prompt: repaint only the face and hair as a Picasso-style cubist painting seen from the front; keep the original photographic background, head size, pose and framing unchanged
no change

nodes.label: held out glossy doll
nodes.question: Does the glossy-doll material effect hold on a held-out draw, including dinov2_large?

params.prompt: make the face and hair a glossy plastic toy doll; keep exactly the same skin colour, hair colour, face shape, expression, pose, lighting, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: computer graphics render
nodes.question: Is photographic rendering itself graded: does a realistic 3D computer-graphics render of the same face cost FFA more than OFA?

params.prompt: render the person as a realistic 3D computer-graphics character from a video game; keep the identity, colours, shading, expression, pose, framing and background
no change

nodes.label: hyperrealistic silicone sculpture
nodes.question: Does a hyperrealistic silicone sculpture, which keeps skin-like pores and colour, spare FFA where marble and plastic did not?

params.prompt: make the head a hyperrealistic silicone sculpture with lifelike skin pores and the same skin colour, displayed as an artwork; keep identity, expression, pose, lighting, framing and background
no change
